Question:
What activities are included in the new employee onboarding period, and how long is that period?

Retrieved context (grouped by document):
=== Document: HR-001 — Employee Handbook ===

[Section: Onboarding Basics]
Chunk ID: 3c0ff18d-c2c6-4655-b39f-b0594d3ea77d
Score: 0.7345
Content:
Onboarding Basics

New employees complete onboarding during their first 10 business days. Required onboarding includes security training, benefits enrollment, department orientation, and access review. Managers are responsible for assigning a buddy and scheduling the first 30-day check-in.

Employees should complete mandatory security awareness training before accessing customer data or production systems.

[Section: Employee Support Channels]
Chunk ID: 9a2e2ee7-48a4-4d0b-ad17-d79dff20c114
Score: 0.5093
Content:
Employee Support Channels

General HR questions should be sent to People Operations. Benefits questions should be sent to the benefits support queue. Security access questions should be sent to IT Support. Performance or role expectation questions should first be discussed with the employee's manager.

=== Document: OPS-001 — Vendor, Travel, and Equipment Operations Policy ===

[Section: Overlap With Other Policies]
Chunk ID: 6e54582d-2f82-4e3b-a832-1117ce09a2e1
Score: 0.8248
Content:
Overlap With Other Policies

Expense reimbursement follows Finance policy. Contract signature follows Legal policy. Device configuration and data security follow IT security policy. When policies overlap, the stricter approval path applies.

[Section: Policy Scope]
Chunk ID: 5feea154-dae9-493a-b80d-a17187b6ab2b
Score: 0.6509
Content:
Policy Scope

This policy covers vendor onboarding, business travel booking, equipment requests, shipping, and operations exceptions. It applies to employees, managers, HR Admins, and IT Admins who request operational support.

Finance controls reimbursement and procurement thresholds. Legal controls contract review. IT controls device security. This Operations policy explains process ownership and routing.

[Section: Exceptions]
Chunk ID: a631c612-3ff0-415b-9908-3f84c7063453
Score: 0.5620
Content:
Exceptions

Operations may approve exceptions for accessibility, business continuity, safety, or customer-critical travel. Repeated exceptions should be converted into a budget request, vendor onboarding request, or role-specific equipment standard.

[Section: Equipment Requests]
Chunk ID: efa74b64-3c3e-4f86-bec3-63476871ca6b
Score: 0.5542
Content:
Equipment Requests

Standard equipment includes a laptop, charger, headset, keyboard, mouse, and monitor. New-hire equipment is initiated by HR Admin and fulfilled by IT Admin. Replacement equipment requires the employee to state whether the request is due to breakage, loss, upgrade, or accessibility need.

Equipment above the standard bundle requires manager approval. Lost equipment that may contain company data must be reported to IT Admin immediately and should not wait for the next business day.

[Section: Vendor Onboarding]
Chunk ID: c83e3811-1cf5-4479-899f-fd76bac98f5a
Score: 0.4899
Content:
Vendor Onboarding

New vendors require a vendor intake request before work begins. The requester must provide vendor legal name, business purpose, expected start date, estimated annual spend, data access level, and contract owner.

| Vendor Risk | Example | Required Review |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Low | Office supplies, training materials | Operations |
| Moderate | Contractor with project files | Operations and Legal |
| High | Vendor processing company or customer data | Operations, Legal, IT Admin |
| Financial | Vendor paid through invoice or purchase order | Operations and Finance |

Vendors may not receive company data, customer data, credentials, or building access until required reviews are complete.

=== Document: FIN-001 — Expense, Procurement, and Reimbursement Policy ===

[Section: Related Policies]
Chunk ID: ae3318d9-3093-40eb-bece-b2aa8ade381f
Score: 0.7034
Content:
Related Policies

Travel bookings must follow the Operations travel process. Vendor contracts must follow Legal approval rules. Software purchases must follow IT security review rules before reimbursement or procurement approval.

[Section: Procurement Thresholds]
Chunk ID: d19f25a2-9f43-402c-97f1-469af8113502
Score: 0.5221
Content:
Procurement Thresholds

Purchases below USD 2,500 may be approved by the employee's manager if the purchase is within the team's approved budget. Purchases from USD 2,500 to USD 10,000 require Finance review before a purchase order is issued.

Purchases above USD 10,000 require Finance review, Legal review if a contract is involved, and department leader approval. Vendors that will process company data must complete the vendor security review before contract signature, even when the spend is below USD 10,000.

=== Document: LEGAL-001 — Contract, NDA, and Data Retention Policy ===

[Section: Contract Approval Process]
Chunk ID: 56f368ca-8cf8-4eec-b828-67bb1302a583
Score: 0.5450
Content:
Contract Approval Process

| Contract Type | Legal Review | Finance Review | Final Approver |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standard customer order form under USD 25,000 ARR | Optional unless redlines exist | Deal Desk | Sales Manager |
| Customer contract with security addendum | Required | Deal Desk | Sales Director |
| Vendor agreement under USD 10,000 | Required if data processing applies | Finance | Department Manager |
| Vendor agreement USD 10,000 or above | Required | Finance | Department Leader |
| Employment-related agreement | Required | HR Admin | People Leader |

No employee may sign a contract on behalf of Northstar unless they are listed in the signature authority register maintained by Legal Operations.
